chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ibn Baqqah, from Saif ibn 'Umayra, from Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The one who enters Mecca free from arrogance, his sin will be forgiven. I said: And what is arrogance? He said: To disdain the creation and stultify the truth. I said: And how is that? He said: That one is ignorant of the truth and vilifies its people.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of arrogance (kibr) in Shia hadith and how does it affect forgiveness in Mecca?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq defining arrogance not merely as pride, but as the active rejection of truth and disparagement of its adherents, a condition that must be purged for the spiritual efficacy of entering Mecca. This specific definition aligns with the Shia emphasis on *kibr* as a cognitive and social vice that blinds the believer to divine guidance, thereby necessitating its removal for the forgiveness of sins during the pilgrimage.
